h: Two Days of Rosh Hashanah: Harsh Judgment and Soft Judgment

p: "We learned: 'And the judgment of His people Yisrael,
דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ' (מְלָכִים א ח, נט).
each day's matter on its day' (I Melachim 8:59).
'Day on its day' — what is it?
אֶלָּא הָנֵי תְּרֵי יוֹמִין דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
Rather, these are the two days of Rosh Hashanah.
Because they are two courts of judgment
the upper judgment, which is harsh,
with the lower judgment, which is soft."
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת ה׳ עִלָּאָה וְה׳ תַּתָּאָה,
That is, the aspect of the upper Hei and the lower Hei,
and both of them dwell in the heart.
For the lower fear as well,
on the verse "when he has no heart" (Mishlei 17:16) —
but has no fear of Heaven.
And Binah, which is "Binah is the heart,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּפֶתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ, הַקְדָּמַת תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר),
as written (in Pesach Eliyahu, Introduction to Tikkunei Zohar),
is when the fear has already entered
the inwardness of the point within the heart.
And these are the aspects of the Written Torah
עַל יוֹם ב׳ שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
regarding the second day of Rosh Hashanah
in the verse "each day's matter on its day,"
which was said by Shlomo HaMelech, alav hashalom,
שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
who was the aspect of the Oral Torah —
the lower Wisdom, the wisdom of Shlomo.
And also the allusion in the Torah:
yet in truth, by Torah law there is no difference;
רַק לִרְמֹז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִדְּרַבָּנָן.
it is only to allude to the Oral Torah, rabbinic law.
has a great root in the Torah.
Therefore, even in the time of the Beis HaMikdash
for the reason that witnesses came
מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ל, ב),
and they are like one long day.
For in truth the two aspects
as it says, "each day's matter on its day":
"'The word of Hashem' (Amos 8:12) — this is halachah";
'הָלוֹךְ וְדַבֵּר' (מְלָכִים ב ב, יא) בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
"'Walking and talking' (II Melachim 2:11) — in words of Torah."
דְּיוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
The first day corresponds to the aspect of the Written Torah,
and then an illumination flows from Above
even into the inwardness of the point in the heart,
from the aspect of the Hidden World,
as stated (in the holy Zohar there)
the Fear of Yitzchak, the concealed judgment, etc.,
and both of them are as one."
And on the second day one comes,
עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
through the revelation of the Oral Torah,
likewise to the aspect of the point in the heart,
"For with much wisdom comes much anger" —
שֶׁכְּדֵי לְהַכְנִיעַ הָרוֹב כַּעַס שֶׁל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
meaning that to subdue the "much anger" of the yetzer hara,
it is done through the "much wisdom,"
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah.
the illumination of the inwardness of the point in the heart,
as stated (in the holy Zohar there)
"'Fortunate is the people who know the teruah;
Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they walk':
the secret of the teruah, as it says,
'You will smash them with an iron rod' (Tehillim 2:9);
and all those who know the secret of the teruah
will merit and draw near to walk
in the light of the countenance of the Holy One, blessed be He;
and this is the primordial light
that the Holy One, blessed be He, stored away for the righteous."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas) — "On the days of Rosh Hashanah the court sets up a throne for the King to judge the whole world… We learned: 'And the judgment of His people Israel, each day's matter on its day' (I Melachim 8:59) — 'day on its day,' what is it? These are the two days of Rosh Hashanah. Why two days? Because they are two courts joined as one: the upper judgment, which is harsh, and the lower judgment, which is soft."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 72b — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?' (Mishlei 17:16)? Woe to Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah but have no fear of Heaven."

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 29b — "Rabbi Levi bar Lachma said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: One verse says, 'a Shabbos, a remembrance of teruah' (Vayikra 23:24), and one verse says, 'a day of teruah it shall be for you' (Bamidbar 29:1). There is no difficulty: here, when Yom Tov falls on Shabbos; there, when Yom Tov falls on a weekday."

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 138b — On "they shall roam to seek the word of Hashem and shall not find it" (Amos 8:12): "'The word of Hashem' — this is halachah; 'the word of Hashem' — this is the End [of days]; 'the word of Hashem' — this is prophecy." Rashi: halachah, as in "to tell you the word of Hashem" (Devarim 5:5), meaning Torah.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 49a — "Rabbi Ila bar Yevarechyah said: Two Torah scholars walking on the road with no words of Torah between them are fit to be burned by fire, as it says, 'And it was, as they went on, walking and talking, behold a chariot of fire' (II Melachim 2:11) — because there was speech; had there been no speech, they would have been fit to be burned." Rashi: talking in words of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas) — "'Blow the shofar at the new moon (bachodesh), at the covered time (bakeseh)' (Tehillim 81:4): 'bachodesh' — this is the soft court, called chodesh; 'bakeseh' — the throne (kes) of the upper world… Further, 'bakeseh' — this is the harsh judgment, the Fear of Yitzchak, a judgment always concealed and not revealed; 'for it is a statute' — the soft judgment; 'a judgment' — the harsh one; and both together — therefore two days."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas) — "'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16): it does not say 'who hear' or 'who blow' the teruah, but 'who know' the teruah — for the wise who dwell in the air of the Holy Land know the teruah, the secret of the teruah… and all who know the secret of the teruah will come near to walk in the light of the face of the Holy One; and this is the primordial light that the Holy One hid away for the righteous."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Toldos Yaakov Yosef, Pinchas — “The first day of Rosh Hashanah is harsh judgment, like shevarim; therefore ‘whom Hashem loves He rebukes,’ and judges him on the second day of Rosh Hashanah, which is soft judgment, like teruah, called ‘dina rafya,’ as explained in the writings. With this understand ‘Fortunate is the people who know the teruah’: more fortunate is the people whose judgment is on the second day, called soft judgment, and they know the teruah, to appease their Creator with the teruah specifically, since it is soft judgment.” Connection: Toldos also divides the two days of Rosh Hashanah into harsh and soft judgment, as the Zohar Rav Tzadok cites does.
